LAND O’LAKES, INC. HAS BEEN WORKING 
ALONGSIDE OUR MEMBER-OWNERS FOR 
MORE THAN 100 YEARS.
Over that time, we’ve seen the ups and 
downs of the agriculture industry, but 
through it all we have held firm in our belief 
that our cooperative approach helps us 
adapt and thrive. This resilience is more 
important than ever as America’s food 
system and farm families navigate an 
unpredictable economic environment. 
We know the stakes are high, and we have 
to meet the moment. At Land O’Lakes, we 
believe the solution is rooted in thinking 
and acting cooperatively. We are in it 
together, from the farm to the plant, and 
from the field to the boardroom. Because 
when we support each other and our 
communities, we all move forward together.

spent 2025 working through a challeng-
ing environment. But during this time, 
the resilience of farm families and the 
value of the cooperative system were once 
again apparent. As the year unfolded, Land 
O’Lakes led a national conversation around 
farm economics, we continued to help our 
communities and one another, and our 
member-owners’ support led to strong 
results for our businesses. 
In 2025, our enterprise approach, paired 
with your partnership, helped deliver a 
strong performance of $16 billion in net 
sales and net earnings of $265 million. 
In fact, each of our businesses delivered 
ahead of their 2025 plans.
In Animal Nutrition, 2025 was marked 
by deeper collaboration with dealers and 
cooperatives, strengthening long‑standing 
partnerships through practical support and 
a shared commitment to serving animal 
owners together, resulting in $72 million 
in pretax earnings. The team streamlined 
operations through major system upgrades 
and cost-saving efforts. The business also 
began the early stages of a strategic shift 
to grow the Purina brand and focus on 
multichannel development.
The Dairy Foods team delivered share 
growth in key products like butter in 2025. 
As demand for products increased, the 
team capitalized by focusing on the growth 
of the dairy case cheese portfolio and by 
launching a series of collaborations to 
strengthen both brand engagement and 
community impact. The business showed 
continued strong performance marked 
in part by manufacturing excellence and 
strong risk management, resulting in $58 
million in pretax earnings.

 1921
To combat rising costs 
and inconsistent quality of 
butter, representatives from 
320 Minnesota cooperative 
creameries form the Minnesota 
Cooperative Creameries 
Association, which would later 
rebrand to Land O’Lakes, Inc. 
1930-1933
As the Great Depression deepens, 
wholesale butter prices sink to an 
all-time low. Land O’Lakes steps in 
and buys 7 million pounds, helping 
shore up the weakening markets.

1937-1944
In the years leading up to and during 
World War II, Land O’Lakes invests in 
the manufacturing of skim milk powder, 
buttermilk powder and casein, and 
converts many of its plants to produce 
wartime essentials for military use. 
By 1944, Land O’Lakes is the nation’s 
largest producer of dry milk powder. 
1950
Congress passes the Margarine Act, 
which repeals federal restrictions on 
margarine coloring, causing a decline in 
butter sales. Land O'Lakes responds by 
creating a highly successful marketing 
campaign that pushes butter sales to an 
all-time high the very next year. 
1970-1987 
Mergers and partnerships with key 
agricultural cooperatives such as Felco 
(1970), Midland Cooperatives (1982) and 
Cenex (1987) turn Land O’Lakes into a 
highly diversified organization that helps 
insulate members from the worst effects 
of the 1980s farm economy crisis. 
1997-1998
Mergers with Atlantic Dairy

welcoming member-owners from

EXECUTING A RESILIENT GROWTH 
STRATEGY IN CANADA
WinField United Canada—like its U.S. counterpart—
combines strong local market insight with world-class 
expertise to support independent ag retailers. In 2025, 
the team successfully recovered from the exit of a major 
supplier, replacing 80% of lost business and delivering 
$86 million in growth through strengthened supplier 
partnerships, post-patent strategies and proprietary 
offerings while reinforcing supply chain reliability.
Growth was led by exceptional performance in adjuvants, 
with 119% year-over-year growth driven by the LockTech® 
family of products. More than 100 spray clinics reached over 
2,000 farmers and 1,200 retail employees, complemented 
by collaborative engagement at the Innovation Center in 
River Falls, Wisconsin. WinField United Canada maintained 
strong momentum and achieved an Employee Engagement 
score of 88%, reflecting a resilient, high-performing team 
and a value proposition that continues to resonate across 
the Canadian market.

EXPANDING RISK MANAGEMENT 
SOLUTIONS AMID VOLATILITY 
Given the volatility of agricultural markets, Land O’Lakes 
has been expanding risk management options to support 
dairy and livestock producers. Following a July 1 rule 
change, we began offering Livestock Risk Management 
to dairy members to help them capitalize on the high 
value of beef. These services are also offered through our 
Animal Nutrition business’ Livestock Risk Services team 
to help a broader network of beef and dairy producers. 
This livestock offering expands our existing risk 
management toolkit, which includes Dairy Revenue 
Protection and Forward Contracting programs to safe-
guard the value of members’ milk production. In 2025, 
the Member Relations and Global Dairy Ingredients 
teams also worked with The Hershey Company to offer a 
unique risk management program for our member-owners 
who supply milk to the chocolate maker.
